A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 24-page versions of the same PALM study, including Appendices A-I. Their text, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 18 LLMs, human assessments, agreement statistics, and empirical analyses of the PALM dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model evaluations, human assessments, and dataset analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The dataset construction, annotation, cross-review, and GPT-assisted instruction categorization procedures remain unchanged. Neither version proposes a different model or algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same 22 Arab countries, 20 topics, MSA, and ten Arabic dialects. No training or evaluation task, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table I.1 retains the same 18 LLMs, and Tables 2, 3, I.3, and I.4 retain their respective comparison subsets. NileChat is newly cited in the introduction but is not added to the evaluated models.

E3.justification: Both retain the 13,559/1,926/1,926 training/public-test/private-test split, greedy decoding, three judge models, and evaluation metrics. Human evaluation still uses 92 MSA samples plus 20 dialectal samples for each of four countries.

E4.justification: The model-size ablation in Appendix I.2.1, annotation-revision analysis in Appendix E, tokenization and lexical analyses in Appendix D, and examples in Appendix H are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or analytical question is introduced.

E5.justification: Both report judge ICC 0.68, human-rater ICC 0.67, and human-versus-judge Pearson correlation 0.76 with p-value below 0.05 and ICC 0.78. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figure 3 changes the displayed instruction-type proportions: Narrative/Descriptive moves from fourth-largest to second-largest, and Directive/Procedural from second to third. This reweighting is unexplained. Model scores in Tables 2, 3, I.3, and I.4 and the model-performance figures remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The metric definitions and Appendix E's revision-difference calculation are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about a human-created, culturally inclusive Arabic dataset covering all 22 countries and its automated and human benchmarking contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model-size, country, and dialect differences remain unchanged. Both retain limitations concerning neighboring-country annotators, incomplete dialect coverage, and automated judges' cultural biases. No explanation accompanies Figure 3's changed proportions.

D1.justification: The guidelines and reproducibility sections redirect readers from the anonymous repository to the named GitHub repository and guidelines file. The abstract already linked to GitHub in v1. v2 also removes the HuggingFace hosting specification from the promised leaderboard; no implementation settings are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and references for NileChat, Peacock, and Pearl. These modestly extend the discussion of Arabic models and cultural benchmarks without substantially changing PALM's positioning or existing dataset comparisons.

P1.justification: v2 changes dataset-name styling to PALM in many passages, updates author affiliations and contact details, and makes limited citation, link, and caption edits. The narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is simplified from three rings to two, with reordered categories and an added appendix pointer; the noun-level breakdowns remain in Figure C.1. Other illustrations are resized, and Table 3 moves from page 8 to page 9. Most appendix displays are visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves Figure 3's legibility and updates citations and resource pointers. However, Figure 3 also changes category proportions and rankings without explaining the reweighting; the analysis description and detailed Figure C.1 remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects an earlier error or introduces one, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
